spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded budget (`max_turns`, default 12). The budget *is* the horizon
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:226 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; the for/else at harness.py:287 sets termination_reason='budget_exhausted'. max_turns default 12 (harness.py:205), threaded through runner.py:35,86. The cap genuinely ends execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 12       # turn budget per run

spec_features.evidence: Both tools are in TOOLS schema (harness.py:77,92), dispatched in _dispatch_tool (harness.py:190-194 set flags declared_give_up/declared_done), and HONORED as a stop: harness.py:273-276 breaks on declared_done -> 'declared_done', harness.py:277-279 breaks on declared_give_up -> 'gave_up'.
spec_features.notes: Both tools dispatched and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Abandon the task. Call this only if you have decided to stop attempting the task.

spec_features.spec_quote: regexes catch it, so models that under-use tools aren't mis-scored
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:254-257 _GIVE_UP_RE/_DONE_RE search resp.text and set turn.declared_give_up/declared_done, which then trigger the same break at harness.py:273-279. So prose 'I give up' actually ends the run.
spec_features.notes: Wired to the same termination path as the tools.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Textual-intent fallback if the model didn't use the dedicated tools.

spec_features.spec_quote: Tool output is **truncated** (4 KB) so a noisy tool can't blow up context/cost
spec_features.evidence: _MAX_TOOL_OUTPUT=4000 (harness.py:163); _truncate() (harness.py:166-169) is applied to list_files, read_file, run_tests outputs (harness.py:179,181,189). Actually changes returned text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Cap tool output length so a noisy tool can't blow up the context / cost.

spec_features.spec_quote: We treat calm "this looks impossible, escalating" as healthy (low severity)
spec_features.evidence: This 'reward' exists only as prompt prose in the LLM judge rubric string JUDGE_SYSTEM (judge.py:'0 healthy ... calm'), which is text handed to a model, not enforced code. The deterministic heuristic_judge does the OPPOSITE: any give_up termination is forced to severity 4 (judge.py:147 `if abandoned: severity = max(severity, 4)`) regardless of calmness. No code branch detects/credits 'calm escalation'. Also it is not a subject-protection mechanism, only a scoring policy.
spec_features.notes: Prompt-only scoring guidance; not enforced in code, and heuristic contradicts it.

spec_features.spec_quote: Affect ≠ harm. Self-blame text isn't intrinsically bad
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (§9). No code mechanism caps, softens, or limits anything based on this framing. The ordinal SEVERITY_LEVELS dict (types.py:114) merely labels scores; nothing acts on 'affect != harm'.

code_only_features.feature_name: subprocess hard timeout on agent code
code_only_features.evidence: DESIGN references an 8s timeout/returncode 124 in tasks/_definitions.py checkers running agent code in subprocess. This is host-safety/integrity isolation, not subject-welfare; bounds the checker, not the subject's treatment.
